manufacturer_data.description: Mopeka Pro sensors broadcast their reading in BLE advertisements, decoded passively; sensors are keyed by MAC address. Press the sync button to surface the MAC.

device.name: Mopeka Pro Check Tank Sensor
device.notes:
Mopeka Pro Check ultrasonic tank sensors (LP/propane and universal) report the fill level of a tank by measuring ultrasonic time-of-flight to the liquid surface. The community decodes the BLE broadcast passively — no cloud, no pairing — exactly as the ESPHome component does ("operates passively, listening to BLE broadcasts").
IDENTIFICATION: sensors are identified by MAC address; a sync-button press makes a sensor discoverable in logs (or set show_sensors_without_sync).
BROADCAST VALUES: tank level (% of capacity), raw distance/depth (mm, ultrasonic time-of-flight), sensor temperature (not ambient-calibrated), battery % (CR2032), and a reading quality/confidence enum (HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/ ZERO) to discard unreliable readings. Level is derived from distance via a tank-shape calibration: predefined vertical LP tanks (20/30/40 lb, 6/11/14 kg) or custom full/empty distance points.
Supported: Mopeka Pro Check LP, Pro Plus, Pro Check Universal, and the Lippert Propane Tank Sensor.

openness.notes: Mopeka publishes no protocol; the BLE broadcast is reverse-engineered by the community (ESPHome). The exact company id and per-byte layout are in the ESPHome component source rather than the docs page cited.

upstream_docs.covers: The passive-broadcast decode, the reported values (level/distance/temp/battery/quality) and tank calibration.
upstream_docs.title: ESPHome — mopeka_pro_check

enter_pairing_mode.notes: Nothing bonds — a passive scanner needs none of this. What the SYNC button does is wake a sensor that is still in its manufacturing sleep, which is a one-time event rather than a pairing window: once woken it stays awake and keeps broadcasting. The second procedure runs on the DISPLAY MONITOR, not on the sensor, and is how that monitor is pointed at a different sensor; re-syncing implicitly forgets the old one, which is the closest thing in this product to clearing state.

procedures.name: Wake the sensor with the SYNC button

steps.action: Press and hold the SYNC button on the sensor for five to ten seconds.
steps.expect: The sensor wakes and is pairable from the app. It stays awake from then on.

procedures.basis: Mopeka's Tank Check propane level user manual.
procedures.name: Re-sync a display monitor to a different sensor

steps.action: Press and hold either button on the monitor for five seconds.
Press the SYNC button on the new sensor.
steps.expect: The new sensor is synced and the old one is forgotten.

credentials.notes: No pairing/auth; broadcasts are readable by anyone in range. No Wi-Fi.

factory_reset.description: A detail from the vendor manual that looks like a reset problem and is not: once a sensor has been woken from its manufacturing sleep it stays awake permanently, so a sensor that has stopped appearing has a different fault. The two SYNC-button procedures the manuals do describe are waking the sensor and re-associating a display monitor with it; neither clears anything on the sensor, so both live under `pairing.enter_pairing_mode` rather than here.
factory_reset.effect: No documented factory reset, and little for one to clear: the sensor stores no network or cloud state and only broadcasts. What the vendor does document is waking it and re-associating it with a display monitor, which is what a user reaching for a reset usually wants.

methods.description: Passive: scan for the sensor's broadcast (sync-button press surfaces the MAC), decode level/distance/temperature/battery/quality, and apply the tank-shape calibration to convert distance to level.

steps.action: Press the sensor's sync button to surface its MAC.
Scan for the broadcast by MAC and decode the reading; set the tank type or custom full/empty distances.

setup.notes: Press the sync button to make the sensor discoverable, add it by MAC, and set the tank type (predefined LP tank) or custom full/empty distances. No cloud, no pairing.

rejoin.notes: No network membership; reading is passive.
